title: Changing Borders of the World
noticeGap: No data: the dataset begins in {year}. No borders are drawn for this period.
noticeSparse: Sparse data: only {n} polity records this year. Empty areas do not mean there were no societies or political organisation.
attribution: Borders: Cliopatria (Seshat), CC BY 4.0, simplified and filtered · Coastlines: Natural Earth · All borders are estimates
coverageAria: Number of polities with data per period, up to {max}
gapTitle: 3500–3401 BCE: not covered by the dataset
noRecordThisYear: The dataset has no border record for this polity in {year}. Its records span {range}.
cardNote: Years describe the span of this dataset's records and are not definitive founding or end dates. Borders are estimates based on historical sources and maps.
srcChanges: Changes made here: removed 385 suzerainty relation records; simplified geometry with mapshaper (about {km} km spacing, shared borders preserved). Contains {rows} records for {polities} polities. Corrected {fixes} endpoints labelled “year 0”.
srcCov1: **3500–3401 BCE: completely empty.** The earliest record is the Sumerian city-states in 3400 BCE, so no borders are drawn before it.
srcCov2: **Data ends in 2024 CE,** and so does the timeline.
srcCov3: **Coverage starts at very different dates by region.** Early periods have only a few polities; the curve on the timeline shows the number of records over time.
srcCov4: **Empty land does not mean uninhabited or without political organisation,** only that this dataset has no polygon there for that year. Non-literate, nomadic and non-state societies are clearly under-represented.
srcRead1: Ancient territories mostly had no precise boundaries. Polygons are estimates from sources and historical maps, often generalising controlled sites or zones of influence, and real power may have faded gradually.
srcRead2: Each polygon applies to a span of years. An unchanged map within that span does not mean the territory did not change. This site never interpolates between records or fills gaps with the nearest data.
srcRead3: The dataset has no per-record border confidence, so no confidence score is shown. Select a polity to see the years its record applies to.
srcRead4: Names, dates and attributions of sovereignty reflect the compilers' choices, and historians disagree in many regions.
srcBase1: Grey land is the modern coastline (Natural Earth 1:50m, public domain), **for orientation only, with no national borders**. Ancient coasts, such as the head of the Persian Gulf, differed.
srcBase2: English names are the dataset's own. Chinese names come from Wikidata (CC0), were reviewed entry by entry with about 300 corrected by hand, and fall back to the dataset name when no reliable translation exists.
